sections.h2: Where is Casa Grande, and what should a seller know about the city?
sections.html:
Casa Grande is a city in Pinal County, roughly halfway between Phoenix and Tucson. It covers 113.9 square miles at an elevation of about 1,381 feet, and the Census Bureau estimates 69,753 residents as of July 1, 2025. That is 29.9% more people than the April 2020 estimates base of 53,705.

The name comes from the Casa Grande Ruins National Monument, which sits in neighboring Coolidge. Casa Grande uses the ZIP codes 85122, 85130, 85193 and 85194. Most working residents commute north toward the Phoenix area or south toward Tucson, and the Census Bureau puts the mean trip to work at 23.3 minutes.

Several roads tie the city to the rest of Arizona:

  • Interstate 8 and Interstate 10
  • State Routes 84, 287 and 387
  • Casa Grande Municipal Airport, which has no scheduled airline service, so most air travelers use Phoenix Sky Harbor or Tucson International

The Census Bureau's median home value for Casa Grande is $303,900, compared with $507,800 in Chandler. That gap, plus the drive to two large job centers, is a large part of what a Casa Grande buyer is weighing.

sections.h2: How did Casa Grande grow, and who employs people there now?
sections.html:
Casa Grande began as a railroad stop and grew into an agricultural town before turning into a commuter and manufacturing city. Southern Pacific Railroad crews settled a spot called Terminus in January 1880, and railroad executives renamed it Casa Grande that September. Fires in 1886 and 1893 destroyed the wooden buildings, the mining boom faded in the 1890s, and farming kept the town alive until it incorporated in 1915.

The 1942 to 1945 Gila River War Relocation Center operated outside town, and the Francisco Grande resort, which the Giants' owner began developing in 1959, hosted the team's spring training. Population climbed from 25,224 in 2000 to 48,571 in 2010 and 53,658 in 2020.

Lucid Motors announced a $700 million plant in November 2016, and the factory opened in November 2020. According to the city's 2024 annual financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, the largest local employers include:

  • Lucid Motors, about 2,450 employees
  • Casa Grande Elementary School District, about 967
  • Walmart Distribution Center, about 850
  • Abbott Nutrition, about 750
  • Banner Casa Grande Medical Center, about 625

New jobs bring new renters and first-time buyers, and they also bring new construction that competes with resale homes. A seller with an older house should expect buyers to compare it with recently built homes nearby.

sections.h2: What do Casa Grande housing and household numbers look like?
sections.html:
Casa Grande is mostly an owner-occupied city with a median home value near $304,000. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures for 2020 to 2024 show the picture below.

Nearly one in five residents is 65 or older, which means many Casa Grande owners have held their homes for a long time. Estates, downsizing and moves to be near family are common reasons these houses come to market.

sections.h2: How do Casa Grande summers and monsoons affect selling a house?
sections.html:
Casa Grande has a hot desert climate, and the weather shapes what buyers look at first. Average daily highs run 105.8 degrees F in June, 106.8 in July and 105.3 in August, and the city gets about 7.91 inches of precipitation in a year. Summer storms in the North American Monsoon bring high winds and heavy rain, and dust storms are common in this part of southern Arizona.

A buyer's inspector is likely to check the roof, the cooling system and exterior finishes with that weather in mind. If you plan to sell as-is, expect the price to reflect any age or damage in those systems. Winters are brief and mild: January highs average 68.7 degrees F and lows 39.1.

sections.h2: What permits and rental rules apply to a Casa Grande house?
sections.html:
The City of Casa Grande Building Division issues permits for construction, alteration, repair, installation, demolition and occupancy-related work. The city lists additions, remodeling, structural work, pools and spas, solar systems, accessory structures and mechanical, electrical, plumbing or gas work as common permit projects, and the Building Division makes the final call. When you are unsure, contact the Development Center before starting. The Building Division is at 510 E. Florence Blvd and answers at 520-421-8630.

If a previous owner added a room, a patio cover or a pool, ask the Building Division for the permit record before you list or accept an offer. Finished work should have a passed final inspection, and a building should not be occupied until any required certificate of occupancy is issued.

Landlords who sell a house they have rented short term should know the city's short-term rental ordinance, No. 1397.05.06, which took effect January 1, 2025. State law at A.R.S. 9-500.39 allows short-term rentals in every Arizona city, so Casa Grande regulates them through a permit instead of banning them. The steps for an owner are:

  • Get a Transaction Privilege Tax license from the Arizona Department of Revenue
  • Notify the Pinal County Assessor's Office of the rental status
  • Apply for the city permit, which costs $115 and renews annually for $115
  • Notify neighbors next door and across the street, and file the attestation within seven business days of getting the permit
  • Post the owner and emergency contact where guests can see it

Operating without a permit can bring civil penalties of up to $1,000 for every 30 days after a 30-day notice. Rules and fees change, so read the city's short-term rental page before relying on these figures.

sections.h2: How are the deed, recording and property tax handled in a Casa Grande sale?
sections.html:
A Casa Grande sale is recorded with the Pinal County Recorder, and the standard recording fee is $30 per document. The county's fee schedule, effective July 1, 2019, says that figure includes the affidavit of property value, extra indexing and a $1 postage charge for mailing the document back.

Arizona law at A.R.S. 11-1133 requires each deed to carry an affidavit of legal value signed by the buyer and seller or their agents. It states the sale price, the date, the parcel number and whether the buyer will occupy or rent the home. The recorder must refuse a deed without a complete affidavit unless the deed notes an exemption under A.R.S. 11-1134, such as a deed of gift or a conveyance made under a court order. Your title or escrow company normally prepares this paperwork.

Property tax on Pinal County parcels with bills over $100 is paid in two halves. The first half is due October 1 and delinquent after 5 p.m. on November 1, and the second half is due March 1 and delinquent after 5 p.m. on May 1. If the date falls on a weekend or holiday, delinquency moves to the next business day, and late interest runs at 16% a year, prorated monthly. Today is past this year's first-half deadline, so ask the Pinal County Treasurer for the current balance on your parcel before closing.

faqs.q: How many people live in Casa Grande?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 69,753 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 53,658 counted in the 2020 census. The city sits in Pinal County between Phoenix and Tucson.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Casa Grande?
faqs.a: The Pinal County Recorder charges $30 for most documents, including a deed, and the fee covers the affidavit of property value and return postage. Your title or escrow company usually pays it at closing.

faqs.q: Does a Casa Grande rental need a city permit?
faqs.a: Yes, any property rented for less than 30 days needs a Casa Grande Short-Term Rental Permit, which costs $115 a year. Owners also need a state Transaction Privilege Tax license and must notify the Pinal County Assessor and nearby neighbors.

faqs.q: When are Pinal County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes over $100 are due in halves, October 1 and March 1, and become delinquent after 5 p.m. on the following November 1 and May 1. Late payments accrue 16% simple interest per year, prorated monthly.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Casa Grande?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Casa Grande Elementary School District, and part is in the Toltec Elementary School District. The whole city belongs to the Casa Grande Union High School District.
